Read one guide at a time. The first two describe THIP access; the last three
run independently with synthetic data and no credentials.

| Guide | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **1. Start here** | Installation, setup and table discovery (this page) |
| [2. Prepare and filter sources](thip-sources.html) | Tables, dates and lazy ICD filtering |
| [3. Retrieve time windows](time-windows.html) | Entry keys, boundaries and batching |
| [4. Flag conditions locally](condition-flags.html) | Custom lists, matching and aggregation |
| [5. Worked cohort example](getting-started.html) | Short end-to-end synthetic analysis |

The remote snippets below are not executed during package builds. Run them in
your authorized THIP R session. Column-name arguments use strings such as
`date = "adm"`; ordinary dplyr verbs handle general manipulation.

## Install or load thipR

If thipR is already available in your THIP R session, use `library(thipR)` and
continue to configuration below. For a new installation, install from GitHub
into your own user library as shown. Installing thipR does not grant THIP
database access.

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("pak")  # Once, if needed

# Use your own library, not the shared platform installation.
lib <- path.expand("~/R/thipR-library")
dir.create(lib, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
.libPaths(c(lib, .libPaths()))
pak::pkg_install("ClickHouseHTTP@1.1.2", lib = lib)  # Tested backend, pinned
pak::pak("Songyosr/thipR", lib = lib)
library(thipR)
```

No source checkout in JupyterLab is required. Installation needs network access,
package dependencies and, where required, a working compiler. thipR requires
exactly ClickHouseHTTP 1.1.2 (the tested backend); installing it explicitly first
keeps the recipe working after CRAN publishes a newer driver. Coordinate missing
platform prerequisites with the maintainers. For a reproducible study, install a tested commit or release using
`Songyosr/thipR@<commit-or-tag>` with an actual reviewed reference.

At the start of later sessions using this custom library:

```{r load, eval=FALSE}
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/thipR-library"), .libPaths()))
library(thipR)
```

Restart an existing R kernel after upgrading an already-loaded package.
A source archive (`.tar.gz`) is another installation option; builds that include
vignettes support `vignette("getting-started", package = "thipR")` locally.

## Configure once, connect each session

```{r configure, eval=FALSE}
library(thipR)
thip_setup()
```

Run this once, in a notebook cell inside your THIP account. You will see, in order:

1. **Two text prompts**: `Database host:` and then `Database username:`. Enter the
   values provided by the THIP team. Port `8123`, database `thip` and scheme
   `http` use their defaults and are not asked for.
2. **A masked password box**: `Database password:`. Typed characters show as dots.
3. **A short pause** while a read-only check connects and then disconnects.
4. **One confirmation line**: "THIP configuration saved with owner-only
   permissions and loaded in this session."

```
thip_setup()
#> Database host: <host provided by the THIP team>
#> Database username: <your database username>
#> Database password: (masked box)
#> THIP configuration saved with owner-only permissions and loaded in this session.
```

Setup saves six `THIP_DB_*` lines to your `~/.Renviron` with owner-only
permissions. In later sessions, call `thip_connect()` only. If the check fails,
nothing is saved and you can simply run `thip_setup()` again.

| Message or symptom | Meaning and what to do |
|---|---|
| "THIP configuration already exists" | Setup was done before. Use `thip_connect()`, or `thip_setup(overwrite = TRUE)` to replace the saved values. |
| "THIP connection verification failed" | The host, username or password is wrong, or the database is unreachable. Nothing was saved; run setup again. |
| "host must be a hostname without a URL, path or credentials" | Enter only the host name, without `http://`, a port or a path. |
| "Input unavailable or cancelled" | A prompt was cancelled or could not be shown. Run setup in an interactive notebook cell. |
| No masked password box outside Jupyter | In RStudio or a terminal, install the `askpass` package. |

The `.Renviron` file is protected by file permissions; it is **plaintext**, not
encrypted. If the platform already supplies the `THIP_DB_*` variables, skip setup.
Never type credentials into notebook code or commit them to a repository. A
Jupyter API token is not used by thipR.

```{r connect, eval=FALSE}
library(thipR)
library(dplyr)
con <- thip_connect()
thip_tables(con)
thip_columns(con, "nhso2568")
```

`thip_connect()` uses two DB threads by default. Row/time limits inherit the
platform settings unless supplied explicitly; overflow raises an error, not
silent truncation. The package does not impose an arbitrary collection cap.
DB thread settings are separate from R's `data.table` thread settings. Metadata
from an individual `_local` shard does not describe the entire distributed table.

## Finish a session

```{r disconnect, eval=FALSE}
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

## Supported API and compatibility

New code should use `tables = ...` and `dplyr::collect()`. Singular
`thip_table(table = ...)` and `thip_collect()` are deprecated compatibility
interfaces. `thip_disconnect()` is also deprecated; use `DBI::dbDisconnect()`.
No connection argument is needed for `thip_filter_icd()` or `thip_window()` when
the source already carries it.

The currently tested backend is ClickHouseHTTP **1.1.2**; connection setup rejects
other versions pending compatibility review. Vignette builds do not certify a
live backend: opt-in read-only smoke scripts in `inst/examples/` cover that path.
Next: [prepare and filter sources](thip-sources.html).
